difficulty_reason: The construction is in the span: endow Z with the reduced induced closed subscheme structure, form the scheme theoretic inverse image Z' of Z in X', and run the cartesian identifications Z' = X' times_X Z = (S' times_S X) times_X Z = S' times_S Z written out in the proof; properness of Z' over S' then follows because it is a base change of the proper Z over S, a named appeal to the base-change stability of proper morphisms. The opening remark that the statement makes sense (f' locally of finite type by the base-change lemma for finite type morphisms) is likewise a named routine check.
